title: More money, same output

predict.q: The economy is at full employment. The money supply doubles; V stays the same. In the **long run**, what happens?

options.s: The price level doubles; real output is unchanged.
options.fb: P = MV ÷ Y = 200 × 4 ÷ 400 = 2.0: double the old 1.0, with Y still at Yf.

options.s: Real output doubles; the price level is unchanged.
options.fb: Output is fixed by resources at full employment. Watch: AD shifts along a vertical LRAS, so only the price level moves.

options.s: Both real output and the price level rise by about half.
options.fb: That would need spare capacity. In the long run all of the extra spending goes into prices.

options.s: The price level rises, but by less than double, because V falls on its own.
options.fb: The theory assumes V is stable; nothing in this task changes V. P doubles.

task: Move the **Money supply** slider from 100 to 200 and watch AD shift right along the vertical LRAS.

target.do: Move the money supply slider to 200, then press Check.

takeaway: With output fixed at full capacity and V stable, more money means a proportionately higher price level.
